Definition: a man in general (singly or collectively)
BiblicalUsage: Enosh is man in general — frail, mortal man, singly or together. Asa prays that man will not prevail against God in 2 Chronicles 14:11, God says He will make the remembrance of men cease in Deuteronomy 32:26, and Isaiah is told to write with a man's pen in Isaiah 8:1. Jeremiah hears the defaming of many and the plots of his familiars in Jeremiah 20:10 — man at his worst, watching for a fall.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe enosh is the Bible's honest word for what we are — weak, short-lived, and prone to plot against each other. I hold that the contrast is the whole point: man is frail, but the LORD who helps Asa is not, and I would rather trust Him than prevail by my own strength.
